grammar.title: Conditional structures: unless, even if, in case (of)
grammar.shortAr: unless = إلا إذا؛ even if للتأكيد؛ in case للاحتياط من احتمال.
points: unless = if not; comma when its clause comes first
even if emphasises that the result will not change
in case = because something might happen; in case of + noun is formal
table: Unless you hurry up, we're going to leave without you.
Even if the company pays me twice as much, I'm going to leave.
Take your umbrella in case it rains.
In case of fire, break the glass.
exceptions: Use present tenses for future; past tenses for hypothetical situations.

vocab.example: I got a lot done today.
I enjoy dealing with a challenge.
I always keep to a routine.

grammar.title: Necessity, obligation and permission
grammar.shortAr: need to، have got to، be supposed to، be allowed to للضرورة والإلزام والإذن.
points: It's necessary/essential to + infinitive focuses on the action
have got to and be supposed to focus on the person
be allowed/permitted to talk about permission; permitted is formal
table: It's necessary to have a driving licence.
This job needs to be done by tomorrow morning.
I'm supposed to wear a hat when I deliver food.
I'm not allowed to go to bed after midnight.
exceptions: Had to is the usual past of have got to.

lessons.title: This or that?

grammar.title: Expressing preferences
grammar.shortAr: would rather + مصدر؛ prefer + اسم/ing + to؛ would prefer + to + مصدر.
points: would rather + infinitive (+ than) for preferences
prefer + noun/-ing + to; would prefer + to + infinitive
table: Zayan would rather cook with electricity than with gas.
I'd rather not answer that question.
I'd prefer to get a takeaway tonight.
exceptions: Use to after prefer: hot weather to cold weather.

vocab.example: I'd prefer to be a chef.
